item.title: A site of my own
item.description: Why matthewfinley.org is a new static site, and what happened to the old pages.
item.content:encoded:
November 15, 2026

A site of my own

matthewfinley.org used to be a handful of separate HTML files. One of them was an office-hours schedule from the fall of 2021. Another was a personal page with a portrait, a few videos, and a photograph of the Eagle Nebula. The front door of the domain pointed at the schedule. That was a reasonable site for a specific semester. It is a poor front door now.

This version is the replacement. It is still static files, because a personal site does not need a build pipeline to say who I am and what I am making. Cloudflare Pages serves the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. A few things that have to remember something, the contact form, the guestbook, and a page-view counter, are Pages Functions. They do nothing useful until the Cloudflare bindings exist, and the pages say so instead of failing in silence.

The sections are the ones I actually have material for. Home and About are the short and long versions of the same biography: computer science student in Cary, NC, about a year and a half left on the degree, builder of games and apps, music under the name sonicrift. Projects names SKYCHARGE, DRIFTHOME, Jingle, and Lake House Manager, and then gets out of the way so the GitHub profile can list everything else that is already public. Music lists the sonicrift catalog and embeds SoundCloud and Spotify alongside it. Videos embed the YouTube account rather than retyping it. Blog is this note and two others. Support is a row of payment methods that stay disabled until the links are real. Contact is an email address first and a form second.

I moved the old files instead of throwing them away. They live under /legacy. The office-hours page is an archive of a semester, not a current invitation. Meeting links that used to be on it are not a way to reach me. The way to reach me is hello@matthewfinley.org.

Two things that will show up later are deliberately absent today. Google AdSense has marked slots and a privacy policy, and it does not have a publisher ID or an ad script. The support buttons have names, and they do not have handles. Both are config. When the values exist, the site can start using them without a redesign. Until then, empty is the honest state.

If you subscribed to nothing before, the RSS feed is the way to follow the notes. There will not be a post every day. There will be a post when there is something to correct or to add, which is a better promise than a calendar I would miss.

item.title: What I'm making
item.description: SKYCHARGE, DRIFTHOME, Jingle, and Lake House Manager, with the public links separated from the builds that are not ready.
item.content:encoded:
November 15, 2026

What I'm making

Four projects are far enough along to have names on the projects page. This note is the same list in paragraph form, with the line between "you can look at the source" and "you can play it" drawn where it actually is.

SKYCHARGE is a flying game. The active work I am willing to announce is a port to Xbox. The source repository is public at github.com/m-fin/skycharge. The port itself is not a public listing. If you open this site looking for an Xbox store link, you will not find one, and that is the current state rather than a broken button. When a playable build exists in public, the card will grow a real link and lose the coming-soon label.

DRIFTHOME is a 3D space-exploration game. Same split: the repository at github.com/m-fin/drifthome is the public artifact, and a playable build is coming soon. I like the project because it is a place to fly through, which is a different itch from SKYCHARGE even though both involve movement. I am not going to invent a backstory on a blog post to make the difference sound bigger than the repositories already are.

Jingle is an alarm clock. The public repository is jingle-ios. An alarm clock does not need a manifesto. It needs to make a noise at the right time. The store listing is coming soon, so the repository is the link and the install button is not.

Lake House Manager is the C++ project. Its link is github.com/m-fin/lake-house-manager. It is not a game and it is not an alarm. It is a manager, and the language is part of the description because that is how I refer to it: the C++ Lake House Manager. I am not hosting a build of it on this domain.

Around those four, the GitHub account m-fin has a longer public history. The projects page loads that list in your browser so I do not have to freeze it into HTML and then forget to update it. Forks are tucked behind a checkbox because a fork is not the same kind of claim as a repository I started. Descriptions in that list belong to the repositories. If one of them disagrees with a sentence on this site, the sentence on this site is the one I am standing behind for the four named projects, and the GitHub text is the repository's own.

Music is the other making. sonicrift stays lowercase and lives on SoundCloud. It is not one of the four cards, because it is not a software release, but it is part of the same habit: finish enough of a thing that another person can press play.

item.title: Bots, robots, drones, and Bitcoin
item.description: The subjects Matthew Finley keeps coming back to, stated without turning them into projects he has not published.
item.content:encoded:
November 15, 2026

Bots, robots, drones, and Bitcoin

There is a difference between a project and an interest, and this site is trying to keep the difference visible. SKYCHARGE, DRIFTHOME, Jingle, Lake House Manager, and sonicrift are projects. They have names and, in most cases, a URL. AI bots, robots, drones, and Bitcoin are interests. They are the subjects I keep returning to while the degree still has about a year and a half on it.

AI bots, for me, means software that can hold a task and use tools, not a promise that I am shipping an assistant. Robots and drones are the physical version of the same curiosity: machines that move because software told them to. Bitcoin is the money-and-protocol version: a system you can run, read, and, if you want, pay someone with. The support page has a slot for a Bitcoin address and a Lightning address for that last reason. Both slots are empty until I put a real address in the config. An interest in Bitcoin is not a wallet printed on a website.

I am not announcing a lab, a fund, a fleet, or a startup around these four words. Cary, NC is the place I am, and the work that is far enough along is the work already linked. If a drone project or a bot becomes a public repository, it will show up in the GitHub list on its own, and I can write about it with the same restraint I am using for the games: what it is, where the link is, and what is still coming soon.

The internship at RIA Advisory sits in a different drawer. June through August 2021, full stack consultant intern. That was a job. It is part of the biography on the about page, and it is not one of these interests. I mention it in the same note only to keep the timeline honest. School is the current chapter. The interests are what I expect to still care about when the remaining year and a half is over.

If you want to talk about any of this, the address is hello@matthewfinley.org. I would rather get a specific question than a generic offer. The guestbook on the contact page is for short public notes, and those notes stay hidden until I approve them, which is a small example of the bot problem: a public form without a check fills up with nonsense. Turnstile is the check, once it is configured.
